Senses.Note: The article is limited to the skull-passing image and its attested question, answer, and staff-action grammar.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：恁麼不恁麼則且置，穿過髑髏一句作麼生？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120) (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)). Speaker: an unnamed questioning monk.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword is inside the monk's third marked question; the following master-said marker begins Chongfan Yu's separate answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1568.xml). Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (Vols. 10–25) (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)). Speaker: Xuedou Chongxian.
Source record (X/X80/X80n1565.xml). Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元). Speaker: Qingfeng Chuanchu.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Qingfeng Chuanchu: The Fengxiang Qingfeng Chuanchu section governs the interview, and the local master-said marker assigns 'pass through the skull, not knowing pain or itch' to Qingfeng Chuanchu.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直饒嫌佛不肯做，被拄杖子穿過髑髏。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X84/X84n1579.xml). Continuation of the Record Pointing at the Moon (續指月錄). Speaker: Juean Mengzhen.

Occurrences.Kwic: 溫州淨居了威禪師因僧問時節因緣即不問慧超佛話事如何師云波斯彎弓面轉黑僧云畢竟如何師云穿過髑髏僧云學人好好借問師云黃泉無邸店今夜宿誰家。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (P/P155/P155n1519.xml). Essential Compendium of the Zen School: Main and Continued Collections (Vols. 13–20) (宗門統要正續集(第13卷-第20卷)). Speaker: Jingju Liaowei.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Jingju Liaowei: The passage names Jingju Liaowei before the exchange, and the second master-said marker governs the exact headword answer.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB198.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueguan (雪關禪師語錄). Speaker: Yingshan Zhiyin.

Senses.Explanation: The retained records use the phrase in a question, in terse answers, and as an action predicated of a staff. Literally, it says 'pass through the skull.' An unnamed questioner asks Chongfan Yu for a skull-passing phrase; Xuedou Chongxian, Qingfeng Chuanchu, and Jingju Liaowei give the image in answers; Juean Mengzhen says a staff passes through the skull.
